B: Stance words zettai, yappari, sasuga, betsu ni, maji de -> C
B: mou ikkai / mou hitotsu, -bai (#2290 'times'), ika/miman (#2734/#16445): tied to numbers and counters, which are excluded list-wide (mou ikkai 'say it again' -> G)

B: Formal or written-leaning degree words with spoken equivalents already listed: hijou ni (非常 #2110), taihen as an adverb, mottomo, issou, sara ni (#1687), kiwamete, sukunakutomo (#1939), yaku (#2575), tashou (#2614), wazuka (#3675), shoushou (#1526, service keigo for chotto)
B: subete (#732): formal synonym of zenbu, mentioned in zenbu's why
B: Variants of listed intensifiers: mechakucha (#1297) and mechamecha (#3664) under metcha; tottemo (#1361) under totemo; sugee (#1510) is a rough form of sugoi (D); honto as a reaction -> G

B: Lower-ranked near-duplicates: issai (#1300, a dramatic 'none whatsoever', covered by mattaku/zenzen), amari ni (mo) (#5513/#3235), taishite (#5363) and taishita (#1113, mostly the G phrase taishita koto nai), chittomo (#3741), sore hodo (#3266), soutou (#1251, overlaps kanari), masumasu (#2113, dondon covers spoken use), yokei (#690, 'unnecessary' sense is D/C)
B: Compositional chunks: hon no sukoshi (ほんの #2207), chotto dake, sukoshi mo + negative; each is built from listed items
B: Narrow totality/part nouns: ichibu (#1749), katahou (#5995), oozei (#1946); pittari (#2786) is covered by choudo; the -me suffix (ookime #6074) is niche
B: ni kuraberu / kurabete (#1477): a verb (H) and written-leaning; the spoken comparison frame is -yori + -no hou ga
C: sukkari (#1314) — means 'completely', so it belongs with totality in B, even though the brief listed it as a starting point.
C: ittai (#819) — only attaches to question words ('ittai nani?'), so it belongs with them in J.
C: isoide (#1222) — the te-form of the H verb isogu; manner -te is already covered at 12-list-te-dependents #1.
C: kichinto (#1580) — a more formal near-synonym of chanto; chanto covers it.
C: sasuga ni (#1098) — nuance-heavy ('understandably / even X can't'); left to sasuga.
C: guuzen (#1011) — a noun ('coincidence'); tamatama covers the adverb use.
C: moshika shitara (#988), hyotto shite (#2612) — variants folded into moshikashite.
C: osoraku (#1784) — the formal / news-register version of tabun.
C: dou yara (#1812) — evidential 'apparently'; belongs to F (certainty/evidence) with rashii / mitai.
C: doumo (#662) — mostly the thanks/greeting use (G); the 'somehow' sense is minor.
C: nandaka (#1462) — filler-like 'kind of / somehow'; overlaps G, and nantonaku covers it.
C: touzen (#746), atarimae (#680) — predicate-type na-adjectives or nouns ('atarimae da'); belong in D.
C: semete (#1148) — the limiting 'at least'; belongs in B.
C: marude (#862) — 'as if', a comparison; belongs in B or I with mitai.
C: motomoto (#1120) — 'originally'; belongs in A.
C: majime ni, shizuka ni (#1514), jouzu ni, kantan ni, hayaku, tadashiku — adverb forms of D adjectives, which come from learning the -ni / -ku derivation.
C: sassato (#1036) — mostly brusque imperatives ('sassato shiro'); hayaku covers it.
C: tsuide ni (#1938) — a 'while you're at it' linker; closer to E.
C: sorezore (#1206) — distributive 'each'; belongs with people words in J.
C: gachi de (ガチ #7029) — slang; maji de already covers it.
C: angai (#2402) — covered by igai to. douri de (#5733) — a realisation reaction, closer to G.
C: Lower-frequency or near-synonym items dropped: nazeka (#1893), aete (#2295), isso (#3093), kaette (#3512), ukkari (#3793, tsui covers it), omowazu (#3808), aru imi (#4266), kihonteki ni (#4814).
C: Manner mimetics and adverbs below the line: jikkuri (#3111), nonbiri (#3406), sotto (#2968), kossori (#2413), omoikkiri (#3668), betsubetsu (#4188), muriyari (#2002).
C: Evaluative adverbs: zannen nagara (#2032), saiwai (#3425), ainiku (#4416) — low frequency and leaning formal.
C: futari de — counter-based (numbers are out of scope); hitori de and minna de cover the manner job.
C: nanka, maa, eeto — fillers, assigned to G by the brief.
C: yoku ('well / often') — belongs to A (frequency) or D (the ii → yoku derivation).
D: taisetsu (大切 #578): merged into daiji (#262), which holds the same slot and is more frequent; see 11-list-adjectives #63
D: yoi (良い #1474) and yoroshii: written/formal and keigo forms of ii; 'yoroshii desu ka' belongs in G set phrases
D: yokatta as the relief interjection, and replies like ii yo, mou ii, daijoubu da yo: these go in G (13-list-exit-battery #98)
D: Contracted and rough variants (sugee #1510, yabee #4269, urusee #1746, tsumannai #2662, mendoi #18552): mentioned in the parent items' notes, not separate cards
D: mijikai (短い #1621): the weaker opposite of nagai and mostly physical; 11-list-adjectives #33
D: shizuka (静か #1715): narrow (places, noise level); 11-list-adjectives #26, 13-list-exit-battery #100
D: tadashii (正しい #1052): in speech, 'that's right' is usually atteru (H) or sou; tadashii leans bookish
D: urusai (#517): narrow noise sense, and 'urusai!' (shut up) is a rude reaction that belongs in G if anywhere; core-vocab i-adjectives
D: abunai (#513): mostly the warning exclamation 'abunai!' (G); 11-list-adjectives #42
D: majime (#1285), kakkoii (#1899), wakai (#505), yasashii's neighbour shinsetsu: describe people only; kawaii and yasashii hold the people slots
D: benri (#3369): applies only to things and services, and its spoken rank is low
D: natsukashii (#1123): has only one trigger (the past); first reserve if D runs short
D: kimochi ii (#2005) / kimochi warui (#1740): transparent compounds of kimochi + ii/warui with a mostly physical sense; kimochi warui ('gross') is a G-type reaction
D: Physical and weather words itai (#336), atsui (#1030/#1990), samui (#1214), nemui (#2976), tsumetai (#1084): physical sensations; 11-list-adjectives #28/#7/#17/#55/#35
D: Physical dimensions tsuyoi/yowai (#310/#970), omoi/karui, akarui/kurai, hiroi/semai, hikui, amai: narrowly physical or only occasionally figurative
D: umai (#246): its senses are covered by jouzu and oishii; the rank is inflated by umaku iku; the 'tasty' sense leans masculine
D: shiawase (#338): rank inflated by drama and romance plots; ureshii covers the in-the-moment 'happy' a learner needs to say
D: heiki (#989): near-synonym of daijoubu
D: jama (#566), meiwaku (#684): behave like nouns; their set phrases (ojama shimasu, meiwaku kakete gomen) belong in G
D: Stance and reply words atarimae (#680), touzen (#746), honki (#559), shoujiki (#496), tashika (#702), hontou (#199), bimyou (#3096), fushigi (#920): C or G

D: Narrower reserves kanpeki (#1243), tokubetsu (#759), muda (#1135), mottainai (#1201), fuan (#857), kibishii (#821), kawaisou (#977), urayamashii (#2394), kuyashii (#1096), erai (#1324; Kansai 'very')
D: Slang dasai (#3663), uzai (#6205), kimoi (#4580): below the cutoff, and rude or slangy
D: subarashii (#1843), suteki (#1102), utsukushii (#1185): written or formal-leaning (suteki leans feminine)
D: Degree and amount words (sugoku, juubun, choudo ii, zenbu, kekkou 'quite'): B; kekkou 'no thanks' is G
D: issho (ni): C/B; hoka: J; chigau: a verb, H
D: Attachment patterns -yasui, -nikui, -sou, -ppoi, -sugiru, -te hoshii: I
D: ikenai, shouganai / shikata nai: G or I
D: Prenominal ookina/chiisana: covered in the ookii/chiisai notes, not separate items
D: Colour adjectives (akai etc.): colours belong in the noun sets; 11-list-adjectives #60
D: yasashii in the 'easy' sense (易しい): merged into kantan
E: shikashi (#380): sounds stiff or written in conversation; demo and desu ga cover it
E: daga (#552): bookish and masculine; dakedo covers it
E: tadashi (#1614), naze nara (#3898), ippou (#1910), aruiwa (#3178), matawa (#8331), moshikuwa (#3716): formal or written register
E: mata (vocab-trainer conjunctions): the 'again' sense belongs to A, and 'moreover' is written
E: kekkyoku (#452), tsuide ni (#1938): outcome and timing words, so they go to A
E: jitsu wa (#249), somosomo (#767), gyaku ni (#1144), mushiro (#1127), sore ni shite mo (#1459): stance adverbs that colour a sentence more than link it, so they go to C
E: -toki, -mae ni, -te kara, -nagara, -ta ato de: time clauses, so they go to A as the brief says
E: sentence-final hearsay -tte: goes to F
E: -tara ii / -ba ii advice and -nakya / -nakereba obligation: go to I
E: -you ni (so that, #158): shares its form with the -you ni suru / -you ni naru patterns, so it goes to I
E: -kawari ni (#1457, instead of): a noun-based pattern with less reach; left for I/B
E: particles to (noun 'and / with') and ya: drilled in kotoba particles; -toka and -ka cover spoken listing here

E: sore nara (#1552), to shitara (#825), you suru ni (#3257) / you wa (#4438), sore ja (#865), sou suru to (#8448): near-synonyms folded into dattara, moshi, tsumari and jaa to avoid duplicate meanings
E: tteka (てか #2194 / ってか #2658, slang) and nde (#3821, casual): noted as variants inside tte iu ka and de/sorede rather than given their own entries
E: nanoni / sore nanoni (#1791), sentence-initial: a variant of -noni, noted there
E: -nakattara / -nakereba (if not): negative forms that follow from -tara / -ba; -nakereba as obligation belongs to I
E: -zu ni: written-leaning twin of -nai de
E: tte iu (called, っていう #178): naming use of the quote tte; covered by -tte or goes to J/I
E: -ba ... hodo (the more ... the more): comparison, so it goes to B
E: ni shite mo (#2105), dotchi ni shite mo (#9505), to iu wake de (not found): weaker reach or no usable rank; reserve level only
F: Auxiliaries that change what the verb means: -tai, -te hoshii, -nakya/-nakucha, -te mo ii, -cha dame, -te miru, the potential, -ou to suru. These go to I.
F: Responses said on their own: sou da ne, sou ka/sokka, sou desu ka, naruhodo, hontou?, maji?, ee. These go to G.
F: Sentence-initial nee/ne ('hey') and ano sa used as an attention opener go to G. Particle sa is kept here.
F: Certainty and stance adverbs (tabun, kitto, zettai, tashika, yappari, hontou ni) go to C. The endings they pair with (deshou, kamo, hazu) are kept here.
F: Connective uses of kedo/kara/noni/node/shi go to E. Only their sentence-final uses (trailing kedo, reassuring kara, regretful noni) are kept here.
F: Keigo requests beyond desu/masu (-te itadakemasen ka, -te itadakeru?, -te kudasaimasen ka, o-V kudasai) are out of scope for the list.
F: onegai / onegaishimasu, and kudasai used with a noun (kore kudasai), are fixed social phrases and go to G.
F: -te mitara? (why not try) is folded into -tara? and -te miru (I). -ba? (sureba?) and -tara dou? are folded into -tara?.
F: -mashou / -mashou ka / -masen ka are folded in as the polite fields of -ou / -ou ka / -nai?. The bare -masu/-mashita paradigm stays with H (verbs carry masu as their polite form).
F: The negative appearance forms -nasasou/-sasou are folded into -sou. daro? (rough tag) is folded into darou. na no? (question) is folded into no?.
F: Copula inflection (datta, ja nai, ja nakatta, deshita) is grammar, not separate endings. Only da itself is kept, as the casual twin of desu.
F: -you ni as a wish (umaku ikimasu you ni) is a low-frequency fixed phrase. -you ni iu (indirect command) belongs to I.
F: beki / beki ja nai is moral or formal register, diagnostic-only in the exit battery. It could go to I if wanted.
F: Written-only certainty forms (-ni chigai nai, de arou, -kamoshirenu, -mai) are excluded.

F: Rare or niche endings (-ttara, mono ka / mon ka 'as if I would', -tamae, -ze yo, -kke na) are excluded, along with combinations already covered by their parts (n ja nai kana, -te hoshii n da kedo, -kamo ne, deshou ne).
F: Dialect endings beyond the single bundled Kansai recognition item are excluded: -hen, -de, -yanen, Hiroshima -ken/-jaken, Tohoku -be, Hokkaido -sho.
F: Hedges such as toka, mitai na (quotative 'like') and nante go to B/C. -tte kanji is kept here as a sentence-ending summary.
G: hai / iie / ee 'yes' (はい #22, いいえ #688, ええ #131): carried as the polite field of un and uun/iya, not as separate items. ee is the soft polite yes and could be added under un if wanted.
G: sou da yo ne (そうだよね #1451): folded into da yo ne (#547), which notes the full form.
G: nani? (bare 'what?', 何 #34): question word, goes to J. Only the repair frames nante? and -tte nani? are kept here.
G: shiranai (知らない #669) 'dunno', chigau (#94) 'no, that's wrong', tasukaru (#542) 'that helps', kamawanai (#3272) 'I don't mind': verbs, go to H. Their reply uses come with the verb entry.
G: betsu ni (#306), ichiou (#779), sasuga (#463), zehi (#1143), yappari: stance adverbs, go to C.

G: yabai (ヤバい #1166), muri (#217), hidoi (#444), saikou (#551), kawaisou (#977), tanoshimi (#869), bikkuri (#1350), kowai, ureshii, omoshiroi: adjectives and adjectival nouns, go to D. Their reaction uses come with the adjective entry; only fixed reply forms (ii yo, ii ne, ii na, ii ya, yokatta, taihen da ne) are kept here.
G: tte iu ka (っていうか #948, というか #2391), tsumari (#499), jitsu wa (#249), jaa as 'well then' (#87): connectors, go to E.
G: chotto as degree 'a little' (#46): goes to B. Only the trailing soft-refusal use is kept here.
G: -te yokatta / -te sumimasen / -te zannen: the evaluative -te frame, goes to I (12-list-te-dependents #15).

G: hora (#145), saa (#263), yoshi (#180), oo (おっ #485), uwa (うわっ #541), waa (わあ #778), fuun (ふーん #601): interjections cut to hold the count. G already has a!, aa, e?, are? and ee for the same jobs, and fuun can sound dismissive.
G: ara (#575): feminine and dated. oi (#127): rough. hai hai (#21197): dismissive. All left out rather than flagged.
G: doumo (#662): its jobs are covered by arigatou and sumimasen, and it is ambiguous between 'hi' and 'thanks'.
G: maa maa (#1073) 'so-so', maa ne (#1789), ma ii ka 'oh well': extensions of maa, left as reserves.
G: nandemo nai (#1152), omatase (お待たせしました #855), shimatta (#3395), maitta (#6016), okkee (ＯＫ #1905): reserves cut on reach. okkee duplicates ryoukai and ii yo, and is slang.
G: dou itashimashite (#4414): textbook phrasing; ie ie (#1047) is what people actually say.
G: sayounara (#2023), baibai (バイバイ #1382): sayounara implies a long or final parting between adults, and baibai is childish slang. jaa ne and mata ne cover goodbye.
G: suman (#1819), warui 'my bad': rough, masculine apologies.
G: sore na (#151338): slang 'so true'; its rank is unusable because the tokenizer splits it.
G: moushiwake arimasen (#786), irasshaimase (#803), kashikomarimashita, osewa ni natte orimasu: keigo beyond desu/masu that the learner only needs to recognise, not produce.
G: akemashite omedetou, yoi otoshi o: seasonal formulas tied to the calendar, which is drilled separately.
G: kanpai (#1054), osaki ni (#2946), odaiji ni (#3401): situational set phrases with low reach.
G: genki? / o-genki desu ka (元気 #297): 'how are you?' is not a routine Japanese opener, and genki itself is in D.
G: Romaji collisions kept on purpose: uun (ううん 'no') vs uun (うーん 'hmm'), and ee (ええ 'yes') vs ee (えー 'aww'). Kotoba's spelling can't tell them apart; audio contour does.

H: Auxiliary uses of these verbs (-teru/-te iru, -te aru, -te miru, -chau/-te shimau, -toku/-te oku, -te kureru, -te morau, -te ageru, -te iku, -te kuru, -te miseru) and i-stem compounds (-hajimeru, -owaru, -tsuzukeru, -sugiru) -> category I; the bare verbs are kept here.
H: Potential and -koto ga dekiru (ikeru, mireru, hanaseru, -eru potential), including slang ikeru! 'it works / tasty' (行ける #985) -> I.
H: Keigo verbs beyond desu/masu (itadaku, kudasaru, irassharu, ossharu, mairu, oru) -> out of scope; their fixed set phrases (itadakimasu, shitsurei shimasu) -> G.

H: Fixed social formulas built on these verbs (ittekimasu, tadaima, okaeri, oyasumi, ki o tsukete as a goodbye, ganbatte as a cheer, otsukaresama, onegai) -> G; ki o tsukeru and ganbaru are kept here as conjugating verbs.

H: Noun+suru compounds: shinpai suru (心配 #210), renraku suru (連絡 #326), yakusoku suru (約束 #412), junbi suru (準備 #532), setsumei suru (説明 #585), benkyou suru (勉強 #729), gaman suru (我慢 #891). The noun is topic vocabulary and suru carries the grammar. shinpai suru (shinpai shinaide) is the strongest reserve if the selector wants one.
H: Verbs inflated by drama plots, with lower everyday reach: shinu (死ぬ #205), ikiru (生きる #211), shinjiru (信じる #266), yurusu (許す #290), mamoru (守る #303), tasukeru (助ける #357), kakusu (隠す #514).

H: Concrete, scene-bound action verbs: kaku (書く #233), yomu (読む #469), yobu (呼ぶ #204), ireru (入れる #222), oku (置く #369), okuru (送る #324), noru (乗る #439), aruku (歩く #526), suwaru (座る #454), tatsu (立つ #610), kiru 'wear' (着る #754), harau (払う #760), uru (売る #687), kasu (貸す #658), kariru (借りる #673), kaesu (返す #460), watasu (渡す #461), akeru (開ける #480), tsukeru 'switch on' (つける #393), kesu (消す #964), sumu 'live' (住む #548). Of these, ireru and oku are the strongest reserves.
H: Emotion verbs used mostly to narrate others: warau (笑う #377), naku (泣く #407), okoru (怒る #381), yorokobu (喜ぶ #519), tanoshimu (楽しむ #713).

H: Narrower reserves for timing, sufficiency and choice: okureru (遅れる #955), maniau (間に合う #904), isogu (急ぐ #733), sumu 'be done / suffice' (済む #671), tariru (足りる #764), nareru (慣れる #946), kimaru (決まる #335), sagasu (探す #391), erabu (選ぶ #378), tsutaeru (伝える #317), au 'fit/match' (合う #563), nokoru (残る #382), ugoku (動く #394), ayamaru (謝る #487). These are useful but less portable than the verbs kept.
H: Further ki- collocations: kizuku / ki ga tsuku (気付く #1083, 気づく #1239). This is the next member of the ki- family after ki ni iru, kept as a reserve.

H: Other transitivity pairs (aku/akeru, shimaru/shimeru, tsuku/tsukeru 'switch on', naoru/naosu, kowareru/kowasu, ochiru/otosu). These are drilled as a system in 13-list-exit-battery B5 (#44-#52) and are topic-bound as single items.
I: -te connective ('and / because / by') -> E connectors; it is a prerequisite of most items here
I: -tara / -ba / -to / -nara as conditionals -> E; only the advice and regret frames (-tara ii, -ba ii, -ba yokatta) are kept here
I: -te mo / -tatte (even if) -> E
I: -nagara, -te kara, -mae ni, -ta ato de, -ta bakari, -teru toko / -te iru tokoro, -ta mama -> A (time clauses and timing)
I: -sou, mitai, rashii, -ppoi, kamo, deshou, hazu, wake, -n da -> F (evidentials and stance endings)
I: -ou ka (offer), -nai? (invitation), -te kureru? / -te kudasai / -naide kudasai as requests, -tara dou (suggestion), -nasai, plain imperatives, prohibitive -na -> F
I: 'X no hou ga ii' comparative preference -> B comparison; advice uses kept as -ta hou ga ii / -nai hou ga ii
I: -masu / -mashita / -masen -> not an item; it is the polite field of every verb item
I: -nakereba naranai / -nakereba ikenai (なければならない #6186) -> stiff and written-leaning; the polite field -nakya ikemasen covers desu/masu obligation
I: -tsuzukeru (keep -ing, 続ける #294) -> reserve cut; -hajimeru and -owaru cover the spoken core of the stem-compound family
I: -dasu, -kiru, -naosu, -au, -kake, -ppanashi -> lower-reach stem compounds that work as lexical items
I: -tagaru / -garu (third-person want or feel; たがる #52822, がる #14551) -> low frequency, recognition only
I: -beki (should, べき #441) -> C stance; moralising register, and -ta hou ga ii covers everyday advice
I: -gachi (tend to, がち #11157) -> low speaking need
I: non-past + koto ga aru ('sometimes does') -> noted under -ta koto ga aru, which shares the ことがある #410 rank
I: -te yaru (blunt or defiant favour) -> rough/masculine variant of -te ageru
I: -te itadaku / -te kudasaru / -te moraemasu ka -> keigo beyond desu/masu, or F requests
I: -te kurete arigatou / -te sumimasen / -te ureshii -> -te plus a G phrase built on the same frame; -te gomen and -te yokatta carry that frame here
I: causative-passive (-saserareru / -sareru, nomasareta) -> recognition only, per the 05-acquisition-order month-8 note
I: -sa nominaliser (takasa, omoshirosa) -> low speaking need
I: -te shou ga nai / -te tamaranai (unbearably) -> C/B degree frames
J: sou as a reply (sou da ne, sou desu ka, sokka) -> G; the manner/pro-form sou is kept here as sou-manner
J: minna meaning 'everything / all of it' -> B; minna is kept here only in its people sense (one primary entry)
J: itsumo (always), the mo-series for itsu -> A (frequency)
J: ano / sono / eto as hesitation fillers, are? (huh?), aa (oh) -> G
J: nanka as a filler or hedge ('like, kind of'), nandemo nai ('it's nothing'), dou mo -> G/C; only the 'something' sense of nanka is kept
J: dou shiyou / dou suru? (what should I do) -> F volitional / G
J: dou demo ii, douse, dou shitemo, dou ni ka (#2957), nantoka (#1078) -> C stance/manner
J: sore de / sore kara / sore ni / sore ja / sou suru to / sou ieba -> E connectors
J: kore kara / sore made / sono ato / sono uchi -> A time
J: konna ni (folded into sonna-ni), dore dake (#1188), hoka 'other/else' (#613), sorezore (#1206), zenbu -> B degree/amount
J: ikura demo (#2178, 'as much as you like') -> folded into ikura's note; may belong in B
J: docchi mo / dochira mo (both), docchi ka / dore ka / dochira ka (#33972 / #183446) -> folded into docchi-demo and docchi; too rare for their own entries
J: koitsu / soitsu / doitsu -> folded into aitsu; kono hito / sono hito -> folded into ano-hito; sono hen / sono atari -> folded into kono-hen
J: itsu kara / itsu made (#8081 / #3150), doko de / doko ni -> question word + particle combinations, not separate items
J: -sama, ano kata, donata-sama, dochira-sama, watakushi, minasama -> keigo beyond desu/masu (set phrases like otsukaresama go to G)
J: nan- + counter (nanji, nannin, nankai, nannen, nan-youbi) and ikutsu as a counting word -> numbers, counters, clock and calendar are excluded
J: korera / sorera (#4556 / #5160) -> plural demonstratives that lean written
